high.title: MSCI Warns Indonesia Could Be Downgraded to Frontier Market — Government Responds
high.summary: MSCI has retained Indonesia in its Emerging Market classification but issued a stark warning that the country could be downgraded to Frontier Market status if two key issues — share ownership structures and indications of coordinated trading practices — are not resolved. A follow-up review is scheduled for November 2026, at which point MSCI will consider reclassification if insufficient progress is made. A downgrade to Frontier Market would likely trigger significant capital outflows from Indonesian equities and weaken the Rupiah.

high.title: Indonesia's Competitiveness Ranking Drops to 48th — Government Investigates Causes
high.summary: Indonesia's ranking in the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking 2026 fell from 40th to 48th out of 70 surveyed countries, raising concerns about the country's investment climate. Coordinating Minister for the Economy Airlangga Hartarto acknowledged the decline and pledged to investigate bottlenecks, highlighting the energy sector — particularly electricity supply — as a critical area of concern. This decline may deter foreign direct investment and signal structural challenges for businesses operating in Indonesia.

high.title: Root Cause of IHSG Plunging 3.56% Despite Indonesia Retaining Emerging Market Status
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed sharply lower at 5,883, down 217 points (3.56%), despite MSCI maintaining Indonesia's Emerging Market status in its Annual Market Classification Review. The negative sentiment was triggered by MSCI opening the possibility of a downgrade to Frontier Market if meaningful capital market reforms are not implemented before the November 2026 review. This represents a significant market risk for investors, as a potential downgrade could trigger large-scale foreign capital outflows from Indonesian equities.

high.title: IHSG Closes Down 3.56% to 5,883
high.summary: The IHSG closed at 5,883, dropping 217 points (3.56%) on Wednesday, after opening in the green at 6,128. Total transaction value reached IDR 15.15 trillion with 26.94 billion shares traded, reflecting high volatility and heavy selling pressure throughout the session. The sharp reversal from intraday highs of 6,171 to a low of 5,876 signals significant investor concern over the MSCI downgrade warning.

high.title: Indonesia's Capital Market Transparency Under MSCI Scrutiny — OJK Chief Pledges Follow-Up Action
high.summary: MSCI has flagged concerns from global institutional investors over the investability of Indonesia's capital market, specifically regarding transparency of shareholding structures and indications of coordinated trading practices. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) chairperson Friderica Widyasari Dewi acknowledged the issues and pledged to follow up on reforms to strengthen transparency, integrity, and competitiveness of the Indonesian capital market. Failure to address these concerns before the November 2026 MSCI review could result in a downgrade from Emerging Market to Frontier Market status.

high.title: IHSG Reverses to Red Zone, Banking Stocks Plunge Collectively
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) reversed course in Session I trading on Wednesday (24/6/2026), falling 1.62% to the 6,002.20 level after briefly touching 6,171.38 at the open. Banking stocks led the decline, with the LQ45 index also dropping 1.45% to 589.763. Transaction value reached IDR 6.73 trillion with 201 stocks advancing and 426 stocks declining, signaling broad market weakness that investors should monitor closely.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Speaks Out on Income Tax Applied to BPJS Employment JHT Withdrawals
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has announced he will coordinate with the Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) to review regulations on income tax (PPh) applied to BPJS Employment Old Age Security (JHT) withdrawals, following widespread public discussion on social media. While the tax rule is not new — established under Government Regulation No. 68/2009 and refined in PMK No. 16/2010 — the minister's willingness to revisit the policy signals a potential regulatory change that could affect millions of workers and the labor welfare landscape.

high.title: Pertamax Price Hike Triggers Rush to Pertalite, Government Boosts Supply to Gas Stations
high.summary: Following a Pertamax fuel price increase, the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) confirmed a consumer migration toward the subsidized Pertalite fuel, prompting BPH Migas to operate 24-hour surveillance of fuel distribution. Pertamina has been instructed to accelerate deliveries to gas stations to prevent long queues and supply shortages. This development has significant implications for the government's fuel subsidy budget and Pertamina's operational costs.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Predicts Continued Decline in Global Oil Prices, State Budget Deficit to Stay Below 3%
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed that Indonesia's state budget deficit will not exceed the 3% legal threshold, citing improving fiscal space. Global oil prices are declining, with Brent crude at $75.07/barrel and WTI at $71.79/barrel, reducing Indonesia's energy subsidy burden. This is positive news for Indonesian investors as it signals fiscal stability and lower inflationary pressure.

high.title: Finance Minister Denies Tax Refund (Restitusi) Being Withheld, Warns Tax Officials Against Misconduct
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya denied allegations that the government is withholding tax refunds (restitusi), stating that Rp 160 trillion in refunds were disbursed in just four months — equivalent to nine months' worth of disbursements in the prior year. He warned that if complaints persist despite higher payouts, it may indicate misconduct by individual tax officers. This has significant implications for businesses managing cash flow and tax compliance in Indonesia.

high.title: Singapore-Flagged Cargo Ship Attacked in Strait of Hormuz, IMO Halts Evacuation Initiative
high.summary: A Singapore-flagged container ship, Ever Lovely, was struck by a projectile — likely a drone — while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy and trade chokepoint. The UN's International Maritime Organization (IMO) has temporarily suspended its ship escort and evacuation initiative in the region. This escalation poses risks to global energy supply chains and shipping costs, with potential knock-on effects on Indonesian commodity exports and energy imports.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Speaks Out on Income Tax Applied to JHT BPJS Employment Withdrawals
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has pledged to coordinate with the Directorate General of Taxation to review the application of income tax (PPh) on BPJS Employment JHT (old-age savings) withdrawals, after the issue went viral on social media. The regulation is not new, having been established under Government Regulation No. 68/2009 and refined in Finance Ministry Regulation No. 16/2010. This development is significant for millions of Indonesian workers and could signal a potential policy review affecting retirement fund taxation.

high.title: Pertamax Price Hike Triggers Rush to Pertalite; Government Boosts Supply to Gas Stations
high.summary: Following a price increase for Pertamax fuel, Indonesian consumers are shifting to the subsidized Pertalite, prompting the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) and BPH Migas to operate 24-hour monitoring and accelerate fuel distribution to gas stations. Pertamina has been instructed to speed up delivery schedules to prevent long queues. This is a critical development for energy sector stability and subsidy burden management, with potential fiscal implications for Pertamina and the government.

high.title: IHSG Closes at 5,896 Level, Drops Below 6,000 Again
high.summary: Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) closed down 1.72% at 5,896.1, falling back below the key 6,000 psychological level after briefly opening higher at 6,010.3. A total of 562 stocks declined versus only 123 gainers, with transaction value reaching Rp 12,735 trillion. This continued weakness signals broad selling pressure and negative sentiment across the Indonesian equity market.

high.title: Asia-Pacific Stock Markets Uniformly Fall as Technology Shares Collapse
high.summary: Asia-Pacific equity markets fell sharply across the board on Friday, driven by a massive sell-off in technology stocks. South Korea's Kospi plunged 5.81% to 8,411.21, Kosdaq dropped 4.10%, and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 fell 4.15% to 69,360.88. The region-wide technology sector rout adds significant external pressure on Indonesian markets and investor sentiment.

high.title: US Dollar Sold Above Rp 18,000 Again at Indonesian Banks
high.summary: The US dollar has strengthened again against the Indonesian Rupiah, with Bloomberg data showing the rate reaching Rp 17,978, while major banks including BRI are already selling dollars at Rp 18,100 at counter rates. The return of the USD/IDR rate to above 18,000 marks renewed pressure on the Rupiah, which is a critical concern for import costs, corporate foreign debt, and overall economic stability in Indonesia.

high.title: IHSG Falls as Much as 2.73% at Midday Trading
high.summary: Indonesia's IHSG dropped sharply by 2.73% to 5,835.11 at the close of the first trading session on Friday, reversing an early morning gain that briefly pushed the index to 6,045.25. The steep intraday reversal indicates strong selling momentum and a deteriorating market outlook. This mid-session decline set the tone for continued weakness into the afternoon close.

medium.title: E-Commerce Platforms Must Announce Service Fee Increases at Least 90 Days in Advance
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has issued Ministerial Regulation No. 3 of 2026, requiring e-commerce platforms to notify sellers of any service fee increases at least 90 days before implementation. The regulation introduces Digital-Based Partnership agreements that lock in fee structures for defined periods, preventing platforms from arbitrarily raising commissions mid-contract. This is a significant regulatory development for MSME sellers and major e-commerce operators such as Tokopedia, Shopee, and Lazada operating in Indonesia.

medium.title: President Prabowo Speaks Out on Police and Military Involvement in Food Security Efforts
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto confirmed that TNI (military) and Polri (national police) are actively involved in Indonesia's food security program, speaking at the 2026 National Farmers and Fishermen Week summit in Gorontalo. The government's food sovereignty agenda continues to mobilize cross-sectoral resources, with key ministers overseeing agriculture, fisheries, and food coordination. Investors in the agricultural and food supply chain sectors should monitor the extent of state-directed intervention in these markets.

medium.title: Sandiaga Uno Becomes Investor in Listed Company MUTU via Private Placement
medium.summary: PT Mutuagung Lestari Tbk (MUTU) is set to receive new strategic investors through a private placement (PMTHMETD), including prominent businessman Sandiaga Salahuddin Uno via PT Samala Serasi Utama and PT Bumi Hijau Sedaya. Former Grab Indonesia CEO and AirAsia Indonesia COO Ridzki D Kramadibrata will also participate as a strategic investor. The entry of high-profile investors may signal growth potential for MUTU and could attract market attention to the stock.

medium.title: Finance Minister Places Regional Staff to Oversee Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) Program Kitchens
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced that regional Ministry of Finance offices (KPKNL and KPPN) will be deployed to periodically monitor Nutrition Service Units (SPPG) under the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) as part of the Free Nutritious Meal program's financial accountability framework. Oversight is set to begin next week, with dedicated monitoring teams formed across all districts and cities. This move reflects the government's effort to tighten fiscal controls over the high-profile MBG program, which carries significant budgetary implications.

medium.title: Husein Sastranegara Airport in Bandung to Operate Starting September 17
medium.summary: PT Angkasa Pura Indonesia (InJourney Airports) has confirmed that Husein Sastranegara Airport in Bandung will resume operations on September 17, 2026, in accordance with a directive from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation at the Ministry of Transportation. The airport will serve scheduled domestic and international commercial flights for both jet and propeller aircraft. This reopening is relevant for aviation sector investors and businesses dependent on Bandung's air connectivity.

medium.title: Indonesia's Energy Ministry Temporarily Halts Coal Exports to Secure Domestic Supply for PLN Power Plants
medium.summary: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) temporarily suspended coal exports to ensure adequate domestic supply of coal with the required calorific value for PLN's power generation needs. The ministry confirmed that coal exports have since returned to normal following improvement in domestic supply conditions. This highlights ongoing domestic market obligation (DMO) enforcement risks for coal producers listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange.

medium.title: Finance Minister Places Local Staff to Oversee Free Nutritious Meal Program Kitchen Financial Accountability
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa will deploy regional Ministry of Finance personnel — via KPKNL and KPPN offices — to regularly monitor the financial accountability of Nutrition Fulfillment Service Units (SPPG) under the National Nutrition Agency's Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program, starting next week. This move responds to a request from the BGN head and aims to strengthen budget controls across all districts and cities. Investors tracking government social spending and fiscal discipline should note this as an effort to improve transparency in one of the administration's flagship programs.

medium.title: Coal Exports Temporarily Halted to Secure Domestic Supply for PLN Power Plants
medium.summary: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) temporarily suspended coal exports to ensure adequate domestic supply of the required caloric-grade coal for PLN's power plants, with exports now resuming normally. The volume withheld was calibrated to PLN's operational needs, and the ministry describes it as a standard regulatory oversight measure. This is relevant to coal mining companies and exporters listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange, as it highlights ongoing domestic market obligation (DMO) enforcement risks.

medium.title: Husein Sastranegara Airport in Bandung to Resume Operations Starting September 17, 2026
medium.summary: PT Angkasa Pura Indonesia (InJourney Airports) has confirmed that Husein Sastranegara Airport in Bandung will resume operations on September 17, 2026, in line with a directive from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. The airport will serve scheduled domestic and international commercial flights for both jet and propeller aircraft. This reopening is significant for the aviation and tourism sectors, as well as for businesses and investors in the greater Bandung area.

medium.title: Panda Bond Issuance Delayed to End of July Due to High Chinese Investor Demand
medium.summary: Indonesia's Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced that the planned issuance of Panda Bonds — yuan-denominated debt securities in China — has been postponed from early July to end of July 2026. The delay was caused by strong interest from Chinese investment managers and major banks who needed additional time to seek internal investment committee approvals. The high demand is considered a positive signal for Indonesia's ability to diversify its sovereign debt financing sources.
